frontPage.headline: Union Cabinet Approves ₹19,934-Crore Package Including Domestic Construction Equipment Ecosystem
frontPage.summary: The Union Cabinet has sanctioned a ₹19,934-crore overall development package, featuring an ₹11,000-crore targeted scheme to manufacture construction and infrastructure equipment domestically. The initiative aims to reduce import dependencies and bolster national supply chain resilience in critical engineering goods.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Crucial for GS-III topics on industrial growth, 'Make in India', and supply chain resilience. Aspirants should note how public capital expenditure is targeted to strengthen local manufacturing capability for heavy machinery.

frontPage.headline: COP31 Negotiations Collapse Amid Deep Fractures Over Fossil Fuel Phase-Out and Climate Finance
frontPage.summary: Global climate negotiations at COP31 ended in a stalemate after over 130 countries, including the EU, rejected a draft agreement that omitted explicit commitments to phase out fossil fuels. Emerging economies like India and China, alongside major oil producers, resisted unfunded transition mandates without binding climate finance commitments from developed nations.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Directly impacts GS-III (Environment & Climate Change Diplomacy). Highlights the persistent global rift between developed and developing nations regarding Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR) and adaptation funding.

frontPage.headline: India Advocates for Inclusive Global AI Governance and Human Oversight in Autonomous Weapons
frontPage.summary: Addressing the United Nations, India warned against using artificial intelligence as a instrument for strategic domination, calling for equitable, democratic governance of technology. India emphasized that legal and moral responsibility over Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) must permanently remain with human operators.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Relevant for GS-II (Global Ethics & UN Bodies) and GS-III (Internal Security & Cyber Tech). Illustrates India's strategic positioning on global technology standards, AI safety, and military ethics.

frontPage.headline: FSSAI Initiates Nationwide Bottled Water Inspection Following Safety Violations
frontPage.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) launched a pan-India surveillance drive to check the quality of packaged drinking water after issuing prosecution orders against major brand samples that failed safety tests for chemical contaminants like bromate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).
frontPage.whyItMatters: Important for GS-II Governance and GS-III Health & Environment. Demonstrates regulatory oversight by statutory bodies like FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

frontPage.headline: Solomon Islands Signs Security Pact with Australia, Restricting Foreign Military Bases
frontPage.summary: The Solomon Islands has officially designated Australia as its primary security partner under a bilateral treaty that expressly forbids the creation of any third-country foreign military base on its territory. The agreement recalibrates security arrangements in the South Pacific after previous security overtures toward China.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Crucial for GS-II (International Relations & Geopolitics of the Indo-Pacific). Shows shifting alignments in Pacific Island Countries (PICs) key to regional maritime security.

frontPage.headline: Supreme Court Quashes High Court Directives for Premature CBI/ED Probes Without Due Process
frontPage.summary: The Supreme Court overturned directives from the High Court that ordered central investigative agencies like the CBI and ED to probe asset declarations without establishing a prima facie criminal offense. The apex court reiterated that judicial power to order central agency probes must be exercised sparingly and with extreme caution.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Significant for GS-II (Structure and Functioning of the Judiciary). Underscores judicial restraint and safeguards against arbitrary orders initiating federal agency inquiries.

gs2.headline: India-Nepal Relations Face Review Over Joint Reports and Border Management
gs2.summary: Debate has resurfaced surrounding the non-acceptance of the India-Nepal Eminent Persons Group (EPG) report on revising bilateral treaties, including the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship. Analysts stress that India must address trade, transit, and border grievances alongside development assistance to build sustainable diplomatic trust.
gs2.whyItMatters: Directly impacts GS-II India's Neighborhood relations. Helps analyze bilateral institutional mechanisms, security interests, and trade ties with Nepal.

gs3.headline: India Maps Landslide Susceptibility Across 4.3 Lakh Sq Km in Risk Mitigation Shift
gs3.summary: India has completed nationwide landslide susceptibility mapping covering 4.3 lakh square kilometers. This initiative marks a strategic paradigm shift from reactive post-disaster relief to proactive disaster risk reduction, leveraging continuous spatial monitoring and hazard zoning.
gs3.whyItMatters: Essential for GS-III Disaster Management topics. Aligns with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction by prioritizing risk mapping and early warning infrastructure.

gs3.headline: Household Solid Fuel Use Drives High Air Pollution in Rural Off-Grid Zones
gs3.summary: A comprehensive study revealed that rural outskirts surrounding major metropolitan areas suffer higher baseline air pollution levels than city centers during winter. Researchers identified domestic combustion of fuel wood, biomass, and dung for heating and cooking—rather than agricultural stubble burning—as the primary factor.
gs3.whyItMatters: Relevant for GS-III Air Pollution and GS-II Clean Energy schemes (e.g., PM Ujjwala Yojana). Highlights gaps in rural clean energy transition policies.

gs3.headline: RBI Maintains Capital Surcharge for Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)
gs3.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reaffirmed the Domestic Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB) status for State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank. Consequently, these institutions must continue maintaining higher Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital buffers to mitigate systemic systemic financial risks.
gs3.whyItMatters: Key concept for GS-III Banking and Monetary Policy. D-SIBs are financial institutions deemed 'too big to fail', requiring additional regulatory capital controls.

gs3.headline: Air Pollution Reprograms Brain Immune Cells Accelerating Cognitive Decline
gs3.summary: Scientific research shows that prolonged exposure to high levels of ambient fine particulate matter causes epigenetic reprogramming of microglia (the brain's resident immune cells), raising the risk of developing neurodegenerative conditions like Alzheimer's by 25%.
gs3.whyItMatters: Useful for understanding environmental health impacts and bio-medical developments under GS-III S&T.

quiz.question: Which of the following financial institutions are currently classified as Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) by the Reserve Bank of India?
options: A) State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, and Bank of Baroda
B) State Bank of India, ICICI Bank, and HDFC Bank
C) HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank
D) State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, and Axis Bank
quiz.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) classifies SBI, ICICI Bank, and HDFC Bank as D-SIBs ('too big to fail'), subjecting them to higher capital buffer requirements.

quiz.question: The 'Little Stint' (Calidris minuta), often observed in Indian wetlands during winter, is a:
options: A) Critically endangered endemic freshwater fish
B) Small migratory shorebird originating from the Arctic tundra
C) High-altitude floral species of the Western Ghats
quiz.explanation: The Little Stint is a tiny long-distance migratory wader bird that breeds in Arctic Siberia and migrates to South Asian wetlands for wintering.

quiz.question: With reference to Autonomous Weapons Systems, which of the following best reflects India's position at international forums like the United Nations?
options: A) Total support for full operational independence of AI in military strike platforms
B) Demand for complete transfer of AI autonomous targeting technology to developing countries
C) Insistence that human accountability and control must be maintained over lethal autonomous weapons
D) Opposition to any civilian deployment of artificial intelligence algorithms
quiz.explanation: India has consistently asserted at the UN that legal responsibility and decision-making over Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) must strictly rest with human operators.

quiz.question: Under the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, national strategies emphasize a paradigm shift towards:
options: A) Exclusively funding post-disaster compensation payouts
B) Proactive risk identification, mapping, and early warning measures
C) Nationalizing all private insurance providers for disaster claims
D) Relying solely on international humanitarian aid agencies
quiz.explanation: Modern disaster management strategies, including India's landslide susceptibility mapping, focus on moving from post-disaster relief to pre-disaster risk reduction and spatial mapping.

schemes.name: Scheme for Enhancing Domestic Construction Equipment Manufacturing
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Heavy Industries / Union Cabinet
schemes.beneficiaries: Domestic equipment manufacturers, infrastructure developers, and industrial workers
schemes.objective: Build local manufacturing capacity for heavy construction machinery, reduce import dependencies, and create domestic industrial employment.
keyFeatures: Incentivization of high-value infrastructure component design and assembly within India
schemes.funding: Centrally sponsored outlay within the overall ₹19,934-crore capital package
schemes.upscRelevance: High relevance for GS-III Industrial Growth, Manufacturing sector policy, and Infrastructure development.

points: India's mapping of 4.3 lakh sq km for landslide susceptibility illustrates the transition from reactive relief to proactive, preventive disaster risk management as envisioned under the Sendai Framework.

mainsEnrichment.topic: Clean Energy & Rural Air Quality Policy
points: Studies showing higher winter pollution in rural outskirts due to domestic solid biomass combustion demonstrate that air pollution mitigation requires last-mile clean cooking energy delivery (LPG/electricity) alongside industrial emission controls.
India's stance at the UN highlights the ethical imperative that lethal force in warfare cannot be delegated to autonomous algorithms, preserving human agency and moral accountability.
